title: Beyond Short Steps in Frank-Wolfe Algorithms
abstract: We introduce novel techniques to enhance Frank-Wolfe algorithms by leveraging function smoothness beyond traditional short steps. Our study focuses on Frank-Wolfe algorithms with step sizes that incorporate primal-dual guarantees, offering practical stopping criteria. We present a new Frank-Wolfe algorithm utilizing an optimistic framework and provide a primal-dual convergence proof. Additionally, we propose a generalized short-step strategy aimed at optimizing a computable primal-dual gap. Interestingly, this new generalized short-step strategy is also applicable to gradient descent algorithms beyond Frank-Wolfe methods. Empirical results demonstrate that our optimistic algorithm outperforms existing methods, highlighting its practical advantages.
problem: Frank-Wolfe algorithms rely on short steps but may not efficiently leverage function smoothness properties for convergence.
approach: Introduce optimistic Frank-Wolfe framework with primal-dual guarantees and generalized short-step strategy optimizing computable primal-dual gap.
contribution: Presents primal-dual convergence proof; empirical results demonstrate optimistic algorithm outperforms existing methods with practical stopping criteria.
